correctness.rationale: A complete finite binary prefix-tree recurrence tracks the longest embeddable prefix of every antisquare. The admissible pruning inequality is necessary, and induction proves exhaustiveness. Optimized C11 execution verified zero hosts at length 4k-2 for k=1..8 and exact k=1..7 counts at length 4k-1. An independent direct literal-target scan agreed at both lengths for k=1..5. The alternating upper bound is proved for every k; reversal/complement orbit and arch-index calculations are justified. No all-k lower bound is claimed.

value.rationale: An antisquare is a structurally natural complement-symmetric pattern family from contemporary combinatorics-on-words research. The shortest common supersequence length of its entire order-k language is a precise covering invariant; completing the first eight minimum-length instances and exact first seven extremal multiplicity, symmetry and ordinary-universality spectra exposes a sharp one-symbol gap from full universality and a quantitative distinction between restricted and unrestricted covering. This is a substantial finite census (up to 128 targets for complete counts and 256 for the length bound) rather than an arbitrary unmotivated sample; no infinite theorem is claimed.
